speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development in respect of the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment 2019, whether the Government will consider (i) increasing the number of lactation rooms from the one lactation room currently required for offices and business parks with a gross floor area of 10,000 sqm and above and (ii) lowering the gross floor area threshold of 10,000 sqm before buildings are required to have at least one lactation room.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The intent of the GFA threshold is to strike a balance between the need for such facilities and the practical implications for smaller buildings, such as efficiency in the use of space.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Notwithstanding this, the developers are encouraged to provide lactation rooms beyond the requirements of the Code, based on the scale of the building and the needs of the building users.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) will continue to study how we can enhance our accessibility requirements, including the provision of lactation rooms, as part of its periodic review of the Code.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Really, we all agree that breast milk is the best food for our babies but we also want our working mothers to return to work and we even incentivise it with the Working Mother's Child Relief.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the two points will be sort of conflicting if we do not allow the working mothers to easily express their milk when they are back at work, if we do not provide enough lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, one, can I ask, for working mothers who work in buildings where the GFA is below 10,000 sqm, where exactly are they going to be able to pump and express their milk?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If they do it in their workplace, there are privacy issues.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, the pumping equipment is actually quite loud.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some of the feedback has been that other colleagues then start to complain about it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, the working mothers are not asking for this big fancy room to pump or express their milk but a small clean place where they can express their milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, whether the Government can step in and provide some grants so that more buildings can provide more lactation rooms for the working mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, I think the Minister of State said that we will review this again in the next periodic review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask when will the next review be because that one lactation room is really very little for the number of working mothers that could possibly work in that building?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I certainly agree with the Member that we should, as much as possible, facilitate our mothers to breastfeed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, it helps with the raising of the child.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the Code Review, in many jurisdictions too, the "one room a building" based on the floor area is, I would say, a base guideline.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is a base rule, rather, not guideline.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is a base rule because we also have to be practical about some of these buildings and how you can retrofit such rooms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: My own experience so far, coming from the private sector, even in a building, you have tenants who, like my previous firm, provided lactation rooms on every floor or most floors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these are on top of the building requirements in which developers may provide one but the tenants themselves could provide more.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have also seen shopping malls with more than one lactation rooms, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I just did a check on my two Ministries.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) has got two in MND Headquarters within the floors that we occupied.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has got five among the two buildings that we occupy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we have not done a survey in terms of the take-up rates out there.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I do think that many building owners have provided more than what the Code requires.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But in setting regulations and codes, it is important that we also take a practical view.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There is funding available for building owners if they wish to undertake this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As of 5 February this year, close to 150 private building owners have tapped on the AF to retrofit their buildings with the accessibility features.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, apart from what we put in the Code, the good thing is that we have seen many private buildings, too, coming on board.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Again, we have to be very practical about how we put Codes up but we support the motion, generally.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The fact that MND and MOM have so many lactation rooms show that there is a need for this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, this is the last supplementary question, which is: when are we going to review this, whether we are going to study this in further detail, see whether in MOM or MND, how many times the lactation rooms are used, whether it is sufficient?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, a really detailed study to look into this issue.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I do think that this could be further promoted to employers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Like I said, tenants themselves, too, have provided lactation rooms for their own officers.
